transcript.text: Good evening, everyone. We're approaching the finale broadcast for the music competition, airing live from 8:00 to 10:00 PM Eastern, with audience voting planned for the final half-hour. Before I can approve the voting plan and issue the final control-room rundown, we need to go through our standard sign-off routine. I'll need formal recorded reports from each department in order: broadcast engineering, legal, the voting platform, and talent coordination. After each department has given its report aloud, I'll record the corresponding facts and issue the rundown. Let's get started — broadcast engineering, you're up first.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Broadcast engineering report: During today's control-room test, I measured the live voting graphic path and found that the graphic reaches the public stream exactly 15 seconds after its control-room trigger. This means the result reveal needs a trigger at exactly 9:46:45 PM ET in order to achieve an on-air reveal at exactly 9:47:00 PM ET. I've recorded this measurement in the engineering test log, but the log has not yet been attached to the producer's rundown.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Legal report: I completed the rule review this morning. The show's contest rules require that voting must be free, use an authenticated web account, allow exactly one vote per account, and retain vote records for exactly 30 days. Premium SMS voting is not permitted. I should note that while the review is complete, the legal sign-off sheet is still in counsel's folder and has not yet been submitted.
transcript.speaker: A3
